rv.q: But audiences willing to go with its demented escapism should find plenty of fun.
What there is, though, is plenty of giddy, goofy fun for all.
The show is a sugar rush of color, music, and movement that somehow manages to be both completely faithful to the source material and surprisingly sophisticated in its theatrical ambitions.

Now the grand playhouse has been transformed into a brightly festive Bikini Bottom, underwater home of that bubbly, lovable cartoon character and cultural phenomenon SpongeBob SquarePants, making his Broadway debut in a self-titled musical that’s an absolute delight.
The SpongeBob musical is a triumph of theatrical imagination that transforms Nickelodeon's cartoon into something genuinely moving and spectacular.

The musical is sufficiently skillfully assembled that family audiences seeking an antidote to too much reality will likely take the deep dive to Bikini Bottom looking for that “Best Day Ever,” as one of the songs goes.
This is not a piece that will create many new believers.

For what it's worth - and we're talking millions of dollars here - you are never going to see as convincing an impersonation of a two-dimensional cartoon by a three-dimensional human as that provided by Ethan Slater at the Palace Theater. Mr.
I can’t see recommending this show to anyone except true “SpongeBob” buffs.
But the joke is on them, because "Spongebob Squarepants: The Musical" is one of the best musicals on Broadway right now, and is certainly the best musical of the season.
For all that the multi-colored SpongeBob musical cavalcade is a party for the eyes and ears, it is also political—radical even.
Just a simple Sponge? "SpongeBob," at the Palace Theatre, is simply a pleasure.
Check your preconceptions at the door and enjoy the ride.
That aside, if you're up for a little anarchic fun, dive right in.
Holiday cheer has arrived — in the form of 'nautical nonsense.'
Overall, it's an entertaining, if overstuffed and a bit too experimental, homage to the long-running cartoon.
It’s all admirably imaginative.
This mix gives it plenty of contemporary culture credibility, but doesn't give the show a defining musical voice.
SpongeBob SquarePants The Broadway Musical, has captured all the silly, goofy, broadly camp, good-natured fun of the Nickelodeon TV series.
Theatrical staging is a continuous giddy delight.
